title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
abstract: arXiv:2610.41970v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. translated_title: 测试时搜索何时有助于世界动作模型？对候选选择与模拟器完整性的实证审计
translated_abstract: 世界动作模型越来越多地采用测试时扩展（test-time scaling），将额外的推理计算投入到候选选择与自适应分配上，以改进控制。只有当候选本身带有可利用的信号、名义上的计算节省能够转化为真实的加速、并且评估保持可靠时，这类收益才可信。我们以“前提优先”的预注册方法，在 Cosmos Policy 和 RoboCasa 上对这三点进行了审计。在干净数据上，学习到的价值选择器比随机选择差 1.66 个百分点；事后（hindsight）oracle 仅提升 1.40 个百分点，且回合级置信区间包含零；82% 的状态下各候选结果完全相同，几乎没有选择空间。Token 剪枝可将每次前向传播的 FLOPs 最多降低 47%，但在部署路径上实测端到端加速最高仅为 1.15 倍（在排除解码的路径上为 1.25 倍），未达到 1.5 倍的目标，而我们的自适应分配实验在统计功效门槛下结果不确定。我们进一步识别……
tldr: 该论文通过预注册的实证审计发现，世界动作模型的测试时搜索收益存疑：候选选择几乎不存在可利用信号（学习到的价值选择器比随机选择还差 1.66 个百分点），token 剪枝虽有 47% 的 FLOPs 节省但实测端到端加速最高仅 1.15 倍、未达 1.5 倍目标，从而揭示测试时扩展所依赖的关键前提往往并不成立。
en_tdlr: Through a pre-registered empirical audit of Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa, this paper shows that test-time search gains are largely unsupported: candidate selection carries almost no exploitable signal (a learned value selector underperforms random by 1.66 pp), and token pruning's 47% FLOPs reduction yields at most a measured 1.15x end-to-end speedup, falling short of the 1.5x target.
